compile.connector_rule: interpolate joint geometry only when support_contact, contact_state, constraint_state, root_state, readiness, guard_authority, and impact_memory match; otherwise hard-cut at causal joins
compile.pipeline: authored decisive ASCII keys -> explicit holds/timing -> deterministic connective motion -> ASCII-only frame render -> MP4 -> self-contained SPA

INFERRED: A block-to-evade transition reads as one defensive action when guard authority is carried across support break rather than dropped and reacquired after the dash.
Compression can store recoil debt that becomes evasive translation after contact release; contact ending does not imply force consequence ending.
Recovery should begin at the first trustworthy rear plant before the torso looks neutral, and final READY should preserve the displacement cost.
All decisive key timing uses STREET_FIGHTER/CAPCOM ONES/TWOS/FOURS because source-authentic timing was not measured.
OBSERVED: TSR exposes Lionel as a single 149-item boss asset with 24 named animation families.

Within that one asset, defensive/evasive state families explicitly coexist: Block, Block Spark, Back Dash Ready, Back Dash, Back Dash Outro, and Idle Hurt; locomotor/action families such as Dash, Dash Skid, Run, Pounce, Punch, Uppercut, plus Death/Defeated provide contrast for support loss, consequence, and re-entry naming.
Block has two listed source items; Block Spark three; Back Dash one; Back Dash Ready two; Back Dash Outro two. The archive page does not provide measured gameplay exposure timing for this pass.
UNKNOWN: Source-authentic chronology between named families, exact gameplay exposure duration, hit-stop/block-stop, root/COM path, contact force, anatomical support ownership, invulnerability windows, and gameplay cancel rules.
No source file bytes were captured in this run; TSR inventory/animation-family evidence was used directly and no source pixels enter the specimen.

principle: GUARD AUTHORITY SURVIVES THE SUPPORT BREAK: a block can hand stored recoil into a backdash only if defensive intent remains readable through unsupported translation and recovery begins at the first trustworthy rear plant; READY returns at a new root address.

consider.CONTEMPT: PASS — rejects the cheap versions: no neutral snap after block, no weightless backdash, no tweened contact invention, no reset-to-origin recovery, no decorative fourth view.
consider.FUNCTION: PASS — defensive intent, force sign, support loss, retreat direction, first trustworthy plant, and displaced re-entry are legible without source character expression.
consider.TASTE: PASS — one specific idea dominates: guard authority is visibly carried through recoil into retreat, instead of becoming generic dodge mush.

noodle_queen.inspect: Reviewed the Tango-satisfied 25-frame Motion Dungeon pass and decisive-key contact sheet as CANDIDATE — NOT APPROVED.
reasons: Impact has a visible consequence path rather than a one-frame flash followed by generic locomotion.
The rear plant earns recovery before posture normalizes, so the cost of defense remains embodied.
The final offset READY makes the specimen worth keeping as a reusable defensive-transition example rather than a technical motion demo.

source.whole_sheet_evidence_basis: Entire TSR asset treated as one evidence corpus. The TSR asset inventory reports 149 items and 24 animation families; the full family set was reviewed, including Block, Block Spark, Back Dash Ready, Back Dash, Back Dash Outro, Idle Hurt, Dash/Skid, Death, Defeated, and multiple action/ready/outro families. No individual source image is embedded or persisted. Source playback timing was not measured.
